([[Daytona Beach, Florida]]) | college = [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] (2020–2022) | highlights = * [[Karl Malone Award]] (2022) * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2022]]) * First-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] (2022) * Big Ten All-Freshman Team (2021) * [[Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament|Big Ten Tournament]] MVP ([[2022 Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament|2022]]) }} '''Keegan Murray''' (born August 19, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]]. ==High school career== Murray played basketball for [[Prairie High School (Iowa)|Prairie High School]] in [[Cedar Rapids, Iowa]].{{cite web |last1=Goffin |first1=Isaac |title=Murray twins excited to compete together at college level |url=https://dailyiowan.com/2020/11/18/murray-twins-excited-to-compete-together-at-college-level/ |website=[[The Daily Iowan]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=November 18, 2020}} As a senior he averaged 20.3 points and 7.2 rebounds per game and was named Metro Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Jeff |title=Prairie’s Keegan Murray named all-Metro boys’ basketball player of the year |url=https://www.thegazette.com/basketball/prairies-keegan-murray-named-all-metro-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/ |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=March 10, 2019}} Murray spent a [[postgraduate year]] at [[DME Academy]] in [[Daytona Beach, Florida]] to gain more exposure.{{cite web |last1=Hensley |first1=Adam |title=Under The Radar: Keegan And Kris Murray's Journey To Iowa Basketball |url=https://www.si.com/college/iowa/basketball/murrays-recruit-041320 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=April 13, 2020}} He averaged 22.1 points and 7.5 rebounds per game, earning most outstanding player honors at the National Prep School Invitational.{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Jeff |title=Iowa commits Keegan and Kris Murray hit home run at DME Sports Academy |url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/iowa-commits-keegan-and-kris-murray-hit-home-run-at-dme-sports-academy/ |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=April 1, 2020}}{{cite web |title=Keegan Murray |url=https://hawkeyesports.com/roster/keegan-murray/ |website=University of Iowa Athletics |access-date=May 24, 2021}} A three-star recruit, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]].{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Jeff |title=Keegan and Kris Murray commit to Iowa basketball, following in their dad's footsteps |url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/keegan-and-kris-murray-commit-to-iowa-basketball-following-in-their-dads-footsteps/ |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=October 21, 2019}} ==College career== [[File:Keegan Murray dunks vs Maryland at Xfinity Center in College Park MD, January 7th 2021 (Abdullah Konte - All Pro Reels Photography) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Murray dunking in January 2021]] On January 2, 2021, Murray recorded a freshman season-high 14 points, nine rebounds, three steals and three blocks in a 77–75 win over [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]].{{cite web |last1=Hlas |first1=Mike |title=Keegan Murray gives Iowa men’s basketball a lot of good things in win over Rutgers |url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/keegan-murray-gives-iowa-mens-basketball-a-lot-of-good-things-in-win-over-rutgers/ |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=January 2, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 7.2 points, 5.1 rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game, earning [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |last1=Emmert |first1=Mark |title=Keegan Murray, Patrick McCaffery will define next year's Iowa basketball season … and beyond |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2021/03/26/iowa-basketball-keegan-murray-patrick-mccaffery-future-stars-new-look-hawkeyes-2021-2022-season/6986297002/ |website=Hawk Central |access-date=May 24, 2021 |date=March 26, 2021}} On November 16, 2021, Murray posted 27 points, 21 rebounds and four blocks in an 86–69 win against [[North Carolina Central Eagles men's basketball|North Carolina Central]]. It was the first 20-point, 20-rebound game by an Iowa player since Bruce King in 1977.{{cite web |title=Murray Goes for 27/21 In Iowa Victory |url=https://hawkeyesports.com/news/2021/11/16/murray-goes-for-27-21-in-iowa-victory/ |website=University of Iowa Athletics |access-date=November 18, 2021 |date=November 16, 2021}} On November 29, he suffered an ankle injury during a 75-74 win over [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], forcing him to miss a game.{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Kennington |title=Iowa basketball star Keegan Murray to miss Purdue game due to ankle injury |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2021/12/03/iowa-basketball-keegan-murray-miss-purdue-game-due-ankle-injury-hawkeyes-big-ten-game/8861063002/ |access-date=December 3, 2021 |work=Hawk Central |date=December 3, 2021}} On December 18, Murray scored 35 points in a 94-75 victory over [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]].{{cite news |title=Murray twins lead Iowa to 94-75 romp over Utah State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401372127 |access-date=February 28, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 18, 2021}} He scored a career-high 37 points on February 13, 2022, in a 98-75 win against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]].{{cite news |title=Murray scores career-high 37 as Iowa pummels Nebraska 98-75 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364439 |access-date=February 28, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 13, 2022}} As a sophomore, Murray was named to the First Team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]],{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|title=2021-22 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |access-date=March 8, 2022}} and won the [[Karl Malone Award]] as the nation's top power forward.{{cite web|url=https://dailyiowan.com/2022/04/02/keegan-murray-wins-karl-malone-power-forward-of-the-year-award/ |title=Keegan Murray wins Karl Malone Power Forward of the Year Award |date=April 2, 2022 |access-date=April 5, 2022 |website=dailyiowan.com |language=en}} On March 29, 2022, Murray declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |date=March 29, 2022 |title=Iowa All-American Murray is entering NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33624259/iowa-sophomore-basketball-player-keegan-murray-entering-nba-draft |access-date=March 29,
